records.context: Two wiring details are load-bearing; both are the same contract :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents, and this function used to get them wrong:
records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two wiring details are load-bearing; both are the same contract :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents, and this function used to get them wrong:
records.translation: Två kopplingsdetaljer är bärande; båda är samma kontrakt som :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` dokumenterar, och den här funktionen brukade göra fel på dem:

records.context: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` uses a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created on the GUI thread. That gives it GUI thread affinity. A queued ``quit()`` goes to the *GUI* event queue rather than the worker queue. The GUI thread immediately enters ``thread.wait()`` during the "drain before closing" behavior in ``ConsolePanel.shutdown``. This blocks the event that would stop the worker and waits for the full timeout even though the worker has finished. ``QThread::quit`` is thread-safe, so the worker thread may call it directly.
records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` is a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created here, on the GUI thread, so it is GUI-affine — a queued ``quit()`` is posted to the *GUI* thread's event queue, not to the worker's. Measured: with a queued connection, a GUI thread that goes straight into ``thread.wait()`` (which is exactly what ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` and every "drain before closing" path does) waits out its whole timeout on a worker that has already finished, because the event that would stop the thread is sitting behind the wait. ``QThread::quit`` is explicitly thread-safe, so calling it inline from the worker thread is correct.
records.translation: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` är en **DirectConnection**. QThread-objektet skapas här, på GUI-tråden, så det har GUI-affinitet — ett köat ``quit()`` postas till *GUI*-trådens händelsekö, inte till arbetarens. Uppmätt: med en köad koppling väntar en GUI-tråd som går direkt in i ``thread.wait()`` (vilket är precis vad ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` och varje "drain before closing" (töm före stängning)-väg gör) ut hela sin tidsgräns på en arbetare som redan är klar, eftersom händelsen som skulle stoppa tråden ligger bakom väntan. ``QThread::quit`` är uttryckligen trådsäker, så att anropa den direkt från arbetstråden är korrekt.

records.context: There is deliberately **no** ``worker.deleteLater``. The worker's affinity is the background execution unit, so a deferred delete is posted into a loop that is stopping, while the panel drops the object's last Python reference from the main GUI execution path — two owners, one object. ``bridge.make_thread``'s ownership essay records the gdb trace (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) and the measurement: 3 crashes in 8 executions. A PySide6 object built in Python is already owned by Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` hold it in ``_retired`` until the independent execution path has exited and free it there, on the independent execution path that holds it.
records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: There is deliberately **no** ``worker.deleteLater``. The worker's affinity is the worker thread, so a deferred delete is posted into a loop that is stopping, while the panel drops the object's last Python reference from the GUI thread — two owners, one object. ``bridge.make_thread``'s ownership essay records the gdb trace (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) and the measurement: 3 crashes in 8 runs. A PySide6 object built in Python is already owned by Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` hold it in ``_retired`` until the thread has exited and free it there, on the thread that holds it.
records.translation: Det finns avsiktligt **ingen** ``worker.deleteLater``. Arbetarens affinitet är arbetstråden, så en fördröjd borttagning postas in i en loop som håller på att stoppas, medan panelen släpper objektets sista Python-referens från GUI-tråden — två ägare, ett objekt. Ägarskapsessän i ``bridge.make_thread`` dokumenterar gdb-spåret (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) och mätningen: 3 krascher på 8 körningar. Ett PySide6-objekt som byggs i Python ägs redan av Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` håller det i ``_retired`` tills tråden har avslutats och frigör det där, på tråden som håller det.

records.context: These are not a procedural sky of point stars — ``cell.png``'s cyan core fills most of the frame and measures 0.236 in the brightest text-line-sized window, which is far too bright to put white-on-nothing text over. So each master is dimmed at build time by a factor solved from the palette: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` returns the brightest a bare window background may be before some role that gets painted straight onto it (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, the status hues) drops below its WCAG minimum, and :func:`solve_dim` scales the image in linear light until the brightest :data:`TEXT_WINDOW`-sized region lands on that number less :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: These are not a procedural sky of point stars — ``cell.png``'s cyan core fills most of the frame and measures 0.236 in the brightest text-line-sized window, which is far too bright to put white-on-nothing text over. So each master is dimmed at build time by a factor solved from the palette: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` returns the brightest a bare window background may be before some role that gets painted straight onto it (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, the status hues) drops below its WCAG minimum, and :func:`solve_dim` scales the image in linear light until the brightest :data:`TEXT_WINDOW`-sized region lands on that number less :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.
records.translation: Det här är ingen procedurell himmel av punktstjärnor — den cyanfärgade kärnan i ``cell.png`` fyller större delen av bilden och mäter 0.236 i det ljusaste fönstret av en textrads storlek, vilket är alldeles för ljust för att lägga vit text direkt ovanpå. Därför dämpas varje originalbild vid byggtiden med en faktor som beräknas från paletten: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` returnerar hur ljus en bar fönsterbakgrund får vara innan någon roll som målas direkt på den (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, statusfärgerna) hamnar under sitt WCAG-minimum, och :func:`solve_dim` skalar bilden i linjärt ljus tills det ljusaste området av storleken :data:`TEXT_WINDOW` landar på det värdet minus :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.

records.context: It reuses ``space``'s cache directory, its size clamps and its "never throw, fall back to something" contract, so from the outside a photo background and a generated one behave identically. What is new is the part that photographs need and procedural pixels do not: a decode budget, an extracted image region policy, and a measured legibility check.
records.label: spacr.qt.imagery#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: It reuses ``space``'s cache directory, its size clamps and its "never raise, fall back to something" contract, so from the outside a photo background and a generated one behave identically. What is new is the part that photographs need and procedural pixels do not: a decode budget, a crop policy, and a measured legibility check.
records.translation: Den återanvänder cachekatalogen i ``space``, dess storleksgränser och dess kontrakt "never raise, fall back to something" (generera aldrig fel, fall alltid tillbaka på något), så utifrån beter sig en fotobakgrund och en genererad bakgrund identiskt. Det nya är den del som fotografier behöver men procedurella pixlar inte gör: en avkodningsbudget, en beskärningspolicy och en uppmätt läsbarhetskontroll.

records.translation: Allt som avgör vad en pixel till slut blir finns i :mod:`spacr.layers`, som inte vet något om Qt. Den här modulen är den del som bara kan finnas med en skärm: en arbetsyta som målar modellens sammansatta bild, en lagerlista som ordnar om den och kontrollerna som anger de egenskaper som modellen redan vet hur den ska respektera.

records.context: The split keeps the model testable. Five later features build on the layer model — ROI shapes read by Measure, a counting points layer, a label brush with timelapse track curation, orthogonal views with dimension sliders, and a synchronised comparison grid — and every one of them is a change to the model with a small widget on top. Putting the compositing rules in a ``paintEvent`` would make all five untestable without a running ``QApplication``.
records.label: spacr.qt.layer_viewer#2

Five later features build on the layer model — ROI shapes read by Measure, a counting points layer, a label brush with timelapse track curation, orthogonal views with dimension sliders, and a synchronised comparison grid — and every one of them is a change to the model with a small widget on top. Putting the compositing rules in a ``paintEvent`` would make all five untestable without a running ``QApplication``.
records.translation: Uppdelningen håller modellen testbar. Fem senare funktioner bygger på lagermodellen — ROI-former som läses av Measure, ett punktlager för räkning, en etikettpensel med kurering av spår i tidsserier, ortogonala vyer med dimensionsreglage och ett synkroniserat jämförelserutnät — och var och en av dem är en ändring av modellen med en liten widget ovanpå. Att lägga sammansättningsreglerna i en ``paintEvent`` skulle göra alla fem otestbara utan en körande ``QApplication``.

records.context: :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview._ZoomView` is the right answer when the thing being shown is a finished pixmap: it scales what it was given. Here the zoom is a property of the world, not of the picture — zooming in means :meth:`spacr.layers.Canvas.zoomed` and a fresh render at the new resolution, which is how the labels layer stays crisp at 8× and how the orthogonal-view item gets its slice sliders for free. So the canvas owns a :class:`~spacr.layers.Canvas` and paints; the array→pixmap step still goes through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.numpy_to_qpixmap`, and file loading through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.load_preview_image`, rather than growing a third copy of either.

records.context: ``clear VRAM`` ``torch.cuda.empty_cache()``, which hands the CUDA driver back the blocks torch reserved and is no longer using, plus releasing any model reference spaCR itself is holding (:data:`MODEL_RELEASERS`). **It cannot reclaim another process's VRAM** — no process can — and it cannot free a tensor an executing spaCR job is still using, which is the point rather than a limitation.
records.label: spacr.qt.resource_cleanup#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``clear VRAM`` ``torch.cuda.empty_cache()``, which hands the CUDA driver back the blocks torch reserved and is no longer using, plus releasing any model reference spaCR itself is holding (:data:`MODEL_RELEASERS`). **It cannot reclaim another process's VRAM** — no process can — and it cannot free a tensor a running spaCR job is still using, which is the point rather than a limitation.
records.translation: ``clear VRAM`` ``torch.cuda.empty_cache()``, som lämnar tillbaka de block till CUDA-drivrutinen som torch reserverade och inte längre använder, plus att alla modellreferenser som spaCR självt håller släpps (:data:`MODEL_RELEASERS`). **Den kan inte återta en annan process VRAM** — det kan ingen process — och den kan inte frigöra en tensor som ett körande spaCR-jobb fortfarande använder, vilket är själva poängen snarare än en begränsning.

records.context: ``clear CPU`` Releases parked background execution units that have since exited (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), lets Qt's global pool retire its idle independent execution paths, and lowers spaCR's own library worker-count limits (torch, OpenCV) to a floor. It retires *idle* capacity only: work that is queued or executing is left exactly where it is.
records.label: spacr.qt.resource_cleanup#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``clear CPU`` Releases parked worker threads that have since exited (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), lets Qt's global pool retire its idle threads, and lowers spaCR's own library thread counts (torch, OpenCV) to a floor. It retires *idle* capacity only: work that is queued or running is left exactly where it is.
records.translation: ``clear CPU`` Släpper parkerade arbetstrådar som sedan dess har avslutats (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), låter den globala poolen i Qt avveckla sina inaktiva trådar och sänker spaCR:s egna trådantal i biblioteken (torch, OpenCV) till en lägstanivå. Den avvecklar bara *inaktiv* kapacitet: arbete som står i kö eller körs lämnas precis där det är.

This machine runs other people's work: a segmentation that starts four seconds sooner is not worth somebody's eight-hour training run, and a tool that decides otherwise on the user's behalf is not a tool anybody can leave running.
records.translation: "Frigör så många resurser som möjligt" får aldrig nå något som spaCR inte äger. Den här datorn kör andras arbete: en segmentering som startar fyra sekunder tidigare är inte värd någons åtta timmar långa träningskörning, och ett verktyg som bestämmer något annat åt användaren är inte ett verktyg som någon kan låta vara igång.

records.context: **No process is ever killed.** Not by name, not by "python processes using a lot of memory", not spaCR's own children. There is no ``os.kill``, no ``signal``, no ``subprocess``, no ``Process.terminate()``, no ``QThread.terminate()`` anywhere in this module or reachable from it. The Qt layer removed ``QThread.terminate()`` outright; a stubborn independent execution path is *parked* by :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, and that is the strongest thing any of this may do.

records.source: **No process is ever killed.** Not by name, not by "python processes using a lot of memory", not spaCR's own children. There is no ``os.kill``, no ``signal``, no ``subprocess``, no ``Process.terminate()``, no ``QThread.terminate()`` anywhere in this module or reachable from it. The Qt layer removed ``QThread.terminate()`` outright; a stubborn thread is *parked* by :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, and that is the strongest thing any of this may do.
records.translation: **Ingen process avslutas någonsin med våld.** Inte efter namn, inte efter "python-processer som använder mycket minne", inte ens spaCR:s egna barnprocesser. Det finns ingen ``os.kill``, ingen ``signal``, ingen ``subprocess``, ingen ``Process.terminate()``, ingen ``QThread.terminate()`` någonstans i den här modulen eller i något som kan nås från den. Qt-lagret tog bort ``QThread.terminate()`` helt; en envis tråd *parkeras* av :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, och det är det kraftigaste något av detta får göra.

records.context: The reconciliation is that the two rules are about different things. The exposure anchor is about a *pixel with nothing in it*; the WCAG limit is about the mean over a **region the size of a line of text** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), which is the point :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` already makes about photographs — every photograph has a white pixel somewhere and it is a bright *patch* that makes a caption unreadable. A 3 px star inside a 202x48 px text window moves that window's mean by a quarter of one per cent; the whole starfield measured on its own comes to 0.0007-0.0067, i.e. 1-11 % of the limit. A 207 px sun disc fills the window completely and cannot.

records.source: The reconciliation is that the two rules are about different things. The exposure anchor is about a *pixel with nothing in it*; the WCAG limit is about the mean over a **region the size of a line of text** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), which is the point :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` already makes about photographs — every photograph has a white pixel somewhere and it is a bright *patch* that makes a caption unreadable. A 3 px star inside a 202x48 px text window moves that window's mean by a quarter of one per cent; the whole starfield measured on its own comes to 0.0007-0.0067, i.e. 1-11 % of the limit. A 207 px sun disc fills the window completely and cannot.
records.translation: Lösningen är att de två reglerna handlar om olika saker. Exponeringsankaret handlar om en *pixel utan något i*; WCAG-gränsen handlar om medelvärdet över ett **område stort som en textrad** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), vilket är den poäng som :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` redan gör om fotografier — varje fotografi har en vit pixel någonstans, och det är en ljus *fläck* som gör en bildtext oläslig. En stjärna på 3 px i ett textfönster på 202x48 px flyttar fönstrets medelvärde med en kvarts procent; hela stjärnfältet mätt för sig kommer upp i 0.0007-0.0067, dvs. 1-11 % av gränsen. En solskiva på 207 px fyller fönstret helt och klarar det inte.

records.context: So the exposure anchor is kept exactly as it was — the sky background is unchanged, to the byte — and the limit is enforced where it is actually violated, by compressing the highlights of the **smooth** layers only (:func:`_compress_highlights`, applied to nebula + galaxy + sun + bloom, never to the starfield). The sun therefore does get noticeably darker, which is the accepted cost; the galaxy is barely touched because it was never the offender; the stars keep white cores and diffraction spikes. :func:`_enforce_legibility` then measures the finished frame with the same :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` used on the photographs and applies whatever residual dim is left, so the guarantee is a measurement and not an argument.

The sun therefore does get noticeably darker, which is the accepted cost; the galaxy is barely touched because it was never the offender; the stars keep white cores and diffraction spikes. :func:`_enforce_legibility` then measures the finished frame with the same :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` used on the photographs and applies whatever residual dim is left, so the guarantee is a measurement and not an argument.

Solen blir därför märkbart mörkare, vilket är den accepterade kostnaden; galaxen påverkas knappt eftersom den aldrig var boven; stjärnorna behåller vita kärnor och diffraktionsspikar. :func:`_enforce_legibility` mäter sedan den färdiga bilden med samma :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` som används på fotografierna och tillämpar den dämpning som återstår, så garantin är en mätning och inte ett argument.

records.context: It must not disappear while the pointer moves toward it. The pointer has to cross the gap between the row and the panel, and a plain leave-event dismissal closes it mid-journey, which makes the Install link unreachable. The hide is a timer, the timer is cancelled on entry, and while it is pending the cursor is checked against the corridor -- the union of the anchor's rectangle and the panel's -- so travelling through the gap re-arms the timer instead of firing it. See :meth:`AvailabilityPanel. _maybe_hide`.

records.context: The panel is a process-wide singleton with two callers. records.context: Return True after writing the PNG displayed by the GUI. Failure of the *related PDF* does not return False. Callers interpret False as "no pixmap, no thumbnail", which would incorrectly remove the figure. records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Returns True once the PNG — the raster the GUI actually displays — is on disk. A failed *sibling PDF* does not turn that into False, and the asymmetry is deliberate rather than sloppy: the callers turn False into "no pixmap, no thumbnail", so reporting a missing export that way would delete the figure from the gallery over a file nothing has asked for yet. It is logged at WARNING instead, and :meth:`FigureQueue._request_pdf_refinement` notices the absent page, says so, and stops waiting for a render that will never arrive.
records.translation: Returnerar True så snart PNG-filen — rastret som GUI:t faktiskt visar — finns på disk. En misslyckad *tillhörande PDF* gör inte om det till False, och asymmetrin är avsiktlig snarare än slarvig: anroparna gör om False till "no pixmap, no thumbnail" (ingen pixmap, ingen miniatyr), så att rapportera en saknad export på det sättet skulle ta bort figuren från galleriet på grund av en fil som ingen ännu har bett om. Det loggas i stället på nivån WARNING, och :meth:`FigureQueue._request_pdf_refinement` märker att sidan saknas, säger det och slutar vänta på en rendering som aldrig kommer.

records.source: That distinction is not cosmetic. ``grna_csv``, ``row_csv`` and ``column_csv`` are declared ``str`` and go straight to ``pd.read_csv``, so rendering them as a list turned a working default into ``['/path/to/barcodes_row.csv']`` the moment the screen was opened and saved. Every run from that file was then refused by the pre-flight -- "column_csv=[...] is a list, but str is expected" -- against a value the user had never typed and could not correct from the panel that wrote it.
records.translation: Den skillnaden är inte kosmetisk. ``grna_csv``, ``row_csv`` och ``column_csv`` är deklarerade som ``str`` och går direkt till ``pd.read_csv``, så att rendera dem som en lista gjorde om ett fungerande standardvärde till ``['/path/to/barcodes_row.csv']`` i samma ögonblick som skärmen öppnades och sparades. Varje körning från den filen avvisades sedan av förkontrollen -- "column_csv=[...] is a list, but str is expected" -- mot ett värde som användaren aldrig hade skrivit och inte kunde rätta i panelen som skrev det.

Antalet noder och nästlingsdjupet är också begränsade (:data:`MAX_NODES`, :data:`MAX_DEPTH`), så ett patologiskt uttryck avvisas vid tolkningen i stället för under en omritning.

records.context: **The whole table, never the filtered view.** ``zscore(area)`` computed over whatever the Local Data Filter currently shows would change every time a slider moved, so the column would not be stable: two charts drawn a second apart would disagree, and an exported CSV would record one arbitrary moment. So :func:`compute` is given the loaded frame and the aggregates (:data:`AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS`) reduce over all of it. Filtering happens afterwards, to the computed column like any other.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.formula#12

records.source: **The whole table, never the filtered view.** ``zscore(area)`` computed over whatever the Local Data Filter currently shows would change every time a slider moved, so the column would not be stable: two charts drawn a second apart would disagree, and an exported CSV would record one arbitrary moment. So :func:`compute` is given the loaded frame and the aggregates (:data:`AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS`) reduce over all of it. Filtering happens afterwards, to the computed column like any other.
records.translation: **Hela tabellen, aldrig den filtrerade vyn.** ``zscore(area)`` beräknad över det som Local Data Filter visar för tillfället skulle ändras varje gång ett reglage flyttades, så kolumnen skulle inte vara stabil: två diagram som ritats med en sekunds mellanrum skulle vara oense, och en exporterad CSV skulle spara ett godtyckligt ögonblick. Därför får :func:`compute` den inlästa tabellen, och aggregaten (:data:`AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS`) reducerar över hela den. Filtreringen sker efteråt, på den beräknade kolumnen precis som på alla andra.

records.context: Two rules apply to what the preview reports.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two rules apply to what the preview reports.
records.translation: Två regler gäller för det som förhandsvisningen rapporterar.

records.context: **Short tracks.** Mean step length and straightness are unstable on a three-point track — straightness is exactly 1.0 for any two-point track, whatever the cell did. So the track-length distribution is drawn beside the velocity plot with the cutoff marked, and the minimum length is a live setting that decides which tracks enter the velocity and straightness numbers.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Short tracks.** Mean step length and straightness are unstable on a three-point track — straightness is exactly 1.0 for any two-point track, whatever the cell did. So the track-length distribution is drawn beside the velocity plot with the cutoff marked, and the minimum length is a live setting that decides which tracks enter the velocity and straightness numbers.
records.translation: **Korta spår.** Medelsteglängd och rakhet är instabila på ett spår med tre punkter — rakheten är exakt 1.0 för varje spår med två punkter, vad cellen än gjorde. Därför ritas fördelningen av spårlängder bredvid hastighetsdiagrammet med gränsvärdet markerat, och minimilängden är en direkt inställning som avgör vilka spår som ingår i talen för hastighet och rakhet.

records.context: The expensive half (reading merged arrays and extracting centroids) runs once in a background execution unit and is **cached** as a point table. Every metric setting — minimum length, max displacement, straightness threshold, and both calibration fields — recomputes from that cached table on the main GUI execution path, instantly.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The expensive half (reading merged arrays and extracting centroids) runs once in a worker thread and is **cached** as a point table. Every metric setting — minimum length, max displacement, straightness threshold, and both calibration fields — recomputes from that cached table on the GUI thread, instantly.
records.translation: Den kostsamma halvan (att läsa sammanslagna arrayer och extrahera tyngdpunkter) körs en gång i en arbetstråd och **cachas** som en punkttabell. Varje måttinställning — minimilängd, största förflyttning, tröskel för rakhet och båda kalibreringsfälten — beräknas om från den cachade tabellen på GUI-tråden, omedelbart.

records.context: Why the scores plot is a GraphCanvas
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_view#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Why the scores plot is a GraphCanvas
records.translation: Varför poängdiagrammet är en GraphCanvas

records.context: A PCA scores plot is a scatter of two continuous columns that a user wants to colour by ``gene``, facet by ``plateID``, and brush to pull a cluster into Annotate. That is the Graph Builder, exactly, with the two columns computed rather than measured. So :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` appends ``PC1…PCk`` to the source frame and :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` is a :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` subclass that draws arrows on top.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_view#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A PCA scores plot is a scatter of two continuous columns that a user wants to colour by ``gene``, facet by ``plateID``, and brush to pull a cluster into Annotate. That is the Graph Builder, exactly, with the two columns computed rather than measured. So :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` appends ``PC1…PCk`` to the source frame and :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` is a :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` subclass that draws arrows on top.
records.translation: Ett poängdiagram för PCA är ett spridningsdiagram över två kontinuerliga kolumner som en användare vill färga efter ``gene``, dela upp i facetter efter ``plateID`` och markera med penseln för att föra över ett kluster till Annotate. Det är exakt Graph Builder, med de två kolumnerna beräknade i stället för uppmätta. Därför lägger :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` till ``PC1…PCk`` i källtabellen, och :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` är en underklass till :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` som ritar pilar ovanpå.

records.context: Everything that took work in the Graph Builder therefore already works here and cannot drift out of step with it: the shared-scale facet grid, the fixed categorical colour order, the large-data policy and its notice, the selection-dims-never-hides rule, and the brush. Because the scores frame carries the object identifier columns, a rectangle dragged around a cluster in PC space publishes a real :class:`~spacr.selection.Selection`, and the UMAP, the laboratory microplate map and the extracted-image-region grid highlight the same cells. Reimplementing a scatter here would have meant reimplementing all of that and getting the brush subtly wrong.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_view#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Everything that took work in the Graph Builder therefore already works here and cannot drift out of step with it: the shared-scale facet grid, the fixed categorical colour order, the large-data policy and its notice, the selection-dims-never-hides rule, and the brush. Because the scores frame carries the object key columns, a rectangle dragged around a cluster in PC space publishes a real :class:`~spacr.selection.Selection`, and the UMAP, the plate map and the crop grid highlight the same cells. Reimplementing a scatter here would have meant reimplementing all of that and getting the brush subtly wrong.
records.translation: Allt som krävde arbete i Graph Builder fungerar därför redan här och kan inte komma i otakt med den: facettrutnätet med gemensam skala, den fasta kategoriska färgordningen, policyn för stora datamängder och dess meddelande, regeln att markering dämpar men aldrig döljer, och penseln. Eftersom poängtabellen bär objektets nyckelkolumner publicerar en rektangel som dras runt ett kluster i PC-rummet en verklig :class:`~spacr.selection.Selection`, och UMAP, plattkartan och beskärningsrutnätet framhäver samma celler. Att implementera ett spridningsdiagram på nytt här skulle ha inneburit att implementera allt det på nytt och få penseln subtilt fel.

records.context: Rows and columns are the **cartesian product** of their structured-data names' levels, empty combinations included, exactly as :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` draws empty panels: a table read by position needs its positions to line up, and one that closes up its gaps tells the reader "there is no row H" when the truth is "row H was measured and is empty". Above :data:`MAX_ROWS` × :data:`MAX_COLS` the product is abandoned for the observed combinations only, and :attr:`PivotResult.notice` says so — an unreadable table is not more honest than a smaller one that admits what it left out.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pivot_spec#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Rows and columns are the **cartesian product** of their keys' levels, empty combinations included, exactly as :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` draws empty panels: a table read by position needs its positions to line up, and one that closes up its gaps tells the reader "there is no row H" when the truth is "row H was measured and is empty". Above :data:`MAX_ROWS` × :data:`MAX_COLS` the product is abandoned for the observed combinations only, and :attr:`PivotResult.notice` says so — an unreadable table is not more honest than a smaller one that admits what it left out.
records.translation: Rader och kolumner är den **kartesiska produkten** av nycklarnas nivåer, tomma kombinationer inräknade, precis som :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` ritar tomma paneler: en tabell som läses efter position behöver att positionerna stämmer, och en tabell som stänger sina luckor säger till läsaren "det finns ingen rad H" när sanningen är "rad H mättes och är tom". Över :data:`MAX_ROWS` × :data:`MAX_COLS` överges produkten till förmån för enbart de observerade kombinationerna, och :attr:`PivotResult.notice` säger det — en oläslig tabell är inte ärligare än en mindre tabell som medger vad den utelämnade.

records.context: Three of those rows were bugs rather than differences of taste. Measure returned after extracting image regions again without a word when no array was loaded, so the button did nothing and said nothing. Timelapse and Motility wired ``QThread.finished`` to ``worker.deleteLater`` and dropped their own reference in the result slot — the pattern :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents as a race, and the one the Mask panel had already been fixed away from — which leaves a running ``QThread`` owned by nobody when the user closes the application view mid-pass. And Measure never told anyone its pass had landed, so no application view could react to an extracted image region preview the way it reacts to the other three.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.preview_contract#56
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Three of those rows were bugs rather than differences of taste. Measure returned from its re-crop without a word when no array was loaded, so the button did nothing and said nothing. Timelapse and Motility wired ``QThread.finished`` to ``worker.deleteLater`` and dropped their own reference in the result slot — the pattern :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents as a race, and the one the Mask panel had already been fixed away from — which leaves a running ``QThread`` owned by nobody when the user closes the screen mid-pass. And Measure never told anyone its pass had landed, so no screen could react to a crop preview the way it reacts to the other three.
records.translation: Tre av de raderna var buggar snarare än smakskillnader. Measure returnerade från sin nya beskärning utan ett ord när ingen array var inläst, så knappen gjorde ingenting och sa ingenting. Timelapse och Motility kopplade ``QThread.finished`` till ``worker.deleteLater`` och släppte sin egen referens i resultatsloten — det mönster som :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` dokumenterar som ett kapplöpningsfel, och det som Mask-panelen redan hade rättats bort från — vilket lämnar en körande ``QThread`` som ingen äger när användaren stänger skärmen mitt i ett pass. Och Measure berättade aldrig för någon att dess pass var klart, så ingen skärm kunde reagera på en förhandsvisning av beskärningar på det sätt den reagerar på de andra tre.

records.context: A **live view** is a panel that re-renders the module's own output from the current settings, on real input, before a processing session. That is Mask, Timelapse, Measure and Motility, and it is what the **Live** toggle opens. The Image UMAP explorer is not one: it makes an already-computed embedding clickable, and no setting changes what it draws. Its toggle therefore says **Interactive**, not Live — the same word had been on both.

That is Mask, Timelapse, Measure and Motility, and it is what the **Live** toggle opens. The Image UMAP explorer is not one: it makes an already-computed embedding clickable, and no setting changes what it draws. Its toggle therefore says **Interactive**, not Live — the same word had been on both.
records.translation: En **direktvy** är en panel som renderar om modulens egna utdata från de aktuella inställningarna, på verkliga indata, före en körning. Det gäller Mask, Timelapse, Measure och Motility, och det är vad reglaget **Live** öppnar. Utforskaren Image UMAP är ingen sådan: den gör en redan beräknad inbäddning klickbar, och ingen inställning ändrar vad den ritar. Dess reglage säger därför **Interactive**, inte Live — samma ord hade funnits på båda.

records.context: **Cancel** and **Stop** are also different words. A live view's Cancel throws the pass away: nothing it produced is kept, because a half -segmented field is not a result. A hyperparameter search's Stop (:class:`spacr.qt.screens.hyperparam.HyperparamPanel`) finishes the trial in flight and keeps every trial already scored, marking the result partial. Same button position, deliberately different verbs, because a user who presses one expecting the other loses either nothing or hours.

records.translation: **Cancel** och **Stop** är också olika ord. En direktvys Cancel kastar passet: inget som det gav behålls, eftersom ett halvt segmenterat bildfält inte är ett resultat. En hyperparametersöknings Stop (:class:`spacr.qt.screens.hyperparam.HyperparamPanel`) slutför det pågående försöket och behåller varje försök som redan har poängsatts, och markerar resultatet som partiellt. Samma knapposition, avsiktligt olika verb, eftersom en användare som trycker på det ena och väntar sig det andra förlorar antingen ingenting eller timmar.

records.context: Nothing on this tab touches a processing-session folder from the main GUI execution path. On one workstation a single ``os.path.exists`` on a path under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep -- did not return within twenty seconds. Every row here carries a folder the user chose, so walking, stat-ing, reading and deleting those folders (the sweep table read on a tab change, ``describe_folder``'s ``os.walk`` inside the delete confirmation, ``shutil.rmtree`` after it, and ``workspace.has_workspace`` while the row menu is built) run on a :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. The one remaining existence check -- which folder to open the chooser in -- is answered from :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`'s cache.

records.source: Nothing on this tab touches a run folder from the GUI thread. Every row here carries a folder the user chose, so walking, stat-ing, reading and deleting those folders (the sweep table read on a tab change, ``describe_folder``'s ``os.walk`` inside the delete confirmation, ``shutil.rmtree`` after it, and ``workspace.has_workspace`` while the row menu is built) run on a :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. The one remaining existence check -- which folder to open the chooser in -- is answered from :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`'s cache.
records.translation: Inget på den här fliken rör en körningsmapp från GUI-tråden. På en arbetsstation returnerade en enda ``os.path.exists`` på en sökväg under ``/nas_mnt`` -- en ``autofs``-montering vars utdelning sov -- inte inom tjugo sekunder. Varje rad här bär en mapp som användaren valde, så att gå igenom, köra stat på, läsa och radera dessa mappar (läsningen av sveptabellen vid ett flikbyte, anropet från ``describe_folder`` till ``os.walk`` inuti raderingsbekräftelsen, ``shutil.rmtree`` efter den och ``workspace.has_workspace`` medan radmenyn byggs) körs på en :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. Den enda återstående kontrollen av om något finns -- vilken mapp väljaren ska öppnas i -- besvaras från cachen i :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`.
